question: A cycle is sold for ₹2,700 at a loss of 10%. Find its cost price.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Loss = 10% → Ratio of CP : SP = 10 : 9

Given SP = 9 units = ₹2,700

1 unit = 2,700 ÷ 9 = ₹300

Cost Price (CP) = 10 units = 10 × 300 = ₹3,000

**∴ The correct option is D.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Given:

Selling Price (SP) = ₹2,700

Loss Percentage = 10%

Formula Used:

Cost Price (CP) = [SP × 100] ÷ [100 − Loss %]

 CP (100%) 
• 
 Loss: 10% SP (90%) ₹? ₹2,700 

Calculations:

⇒ CP = [2,700 × 100] ÷ [100 − 10]

⇒ CP = 2,70,000 ÷ 90

⇒ CP = 3,000

**∴ The correct option is D.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Profit Percentage

Profit % = [Profit ÷ CP] × 100, where Profit = SP − CP.

Successive Discounts

If two successive discounts of d₁% and d₂% are given, then net discount = [d₁ + d₂ − (d₁ × d₂) ÷ 100]%.

Marked Price and CP Relation

CP ÷ MP = [100 − Discount%] ÷ [100 + Profit%].
